analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts (scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py and scripts/test-ci-tested-tree.py). Neither touches provider runtime, the coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, or cache storage code, so the provider/native-runtime threat model assets (A-001..A-020) and boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013/014) are not directly affected.

Head-side changes to test-ci-component-paths.py:
- Asserts the new opt-in `run-ci` / `run-gpu-ci` label gating and an `unlabel` job (head lines 336-349).
- PRs into master now route by diff, not full fan-out (head 277-297).
- A `cluster_gpu` gate is tested for its event, ref and label combinations (head 411-436).
- Public-workflow assertions are retained: no secrets., environment:, id-token: or repository: (head 365-369), and no pull_request_target in component-changes.yml (head 466).

Security-relevant observation: weaker PR test coverage on master-bound PRs is a CI policy choice. Master pushes still select every component (head 284-287), and the tested-tree dedupe still checks the tree, a successful run, the same repo and the workflow path.

test-ci-tested-tree.py adds tests for tree-only records (`ci-tested-tree-...`) so a squash-merge push can skip after the PR's tested tree. The tests also pin the fail-closed cases: wrong tree, failed run, fork head repository, wrong workflow path, and insufficient component coverage. A pull request must not match a tree-only record.

The implementations (scripts/ci-tested-tree.py, the workflows) are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that skipping on a tree record is safe in production. These are only tests. The next pass should check that tree-record skipping requires a run from the trusted repo and workflow, and that the label-triggered `unlabel` job uses minimal permissions. This is not a verified regression.
